Hi Marissa / Laura,

We're lining up the logistics for the Tokyo exec workshop (week of 2026-12-14). Quick checklist items I need from you both so we can trigger invitation letters and secure any expedited consulate windows: 

- Final attendee list (full legal names as on passport, DOB, nationality) — due EOD Fri 11/6.
- Passport scans (photo page) for any non-Japan-national attendees with < 6 months validity — flag those who need renewal.
- Indicate whether attendees require invitation letters for visa or COE paperwork (we anticipate business visa only).
- Confirm whether we want Redwood to route attendees through our visa partner (Alicia) for expedited bookings.

I will draft the formal invitation letter templates and send to Kumon (host) for signature. Planning notes: most Tokyo consulates have 3–4 week appointment lead times right now; if anyone has < 3 months on passport validity we should prioritize renewals.

Thanks — I’ll compile everything into a single packet for Naoki at Kumon.

Dylan Brooks

Hi Naoki — great speaking last week.

Kumon's hosting is hugely appreciated. To keep our teams moving on visas, can you please: 

1) Provide a signed letter of invitation on Kumon letterhead for the Redwood/Kumon Executive Workshop (Dec 14–16) that includes: attendee full names, passport numbers, purpose of visit (business workshop), host contact, and planned local address for the stay.

2) Share the venue's confirmation / provisional invoice (for visa packet).

We plan to group attendees into a single packet where possible (Redwood will provide passport scans). If Kumon prefers, we can supply a draft invitation for your signature — I have a template ready.

We'd also appreciate any guidance on whether a work / temporary COE is required versus a standard business visa for attendees coming from India and Brazil.

If you can return the signed invite and venue confirmation by 11/16 it will keep everyone on track for consulate appointments.

Best,
Dylan

Dylan — thanks for the details. Apologies for the short delay. We can provide a signed invitation on Kumon letterhead.

Please find attached:
- Redwood_Invitation_Letter_Kumon_202611.pdf (signed)
- Tentative_Agenda_Tokyo_Workshop.xlsx (venue slots marked)

Notes:
- For business short-term visits (3–6 days), a business visa is normally sufficient. A Certificate of Eligibility (COE) is not required for short-term business visits.
- For Brazilian passport holders, the Tokyo consulate requires an additional company registration extract; we attached sample wording.
- Venue confirmation: Yuki included the provisional invoice separately.

On consulate timing — several embassies are experiencing appointment backlogs through early December. If any attendee does not have 6 months validity on their passport from date of arrival (Dec 14) they will be denied boarding; please flag anyone under 6 months immediately.

Best regards,

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

Thanks for looping us in. GlobalEvents Visa Services can support the group with:

- Consolidated visa packet review (we check all docs before submission).
- Consulate appointment sourcing (we maintain relationships across APAC consulates and can secure cancellations).
- Expedited courier for passport submission/return (48–72 hours in metro areas).

Typical timeline if we start this week: 
- Packet finalization: 2 business days after we receive passport scans + signed invitation letters.
- Consulate appointment window: 7–21 days depending on nationality; we can often find cancellations within 5–10 days.
- Expedited service fee: USD 220 per passport (includes courier + appointment sourcing).

Required docs (we'll generate a checklist for each attendee): passport scan, signed invitation, company registration extract (for certain nationalities), proof of return travel, accommodation confirmation, and the tentative agenda.

We can prepare individual PDF visa-kits (one per attendee) for upload to embassy portals. If you'd like, we'll send a sample kit for your review.

Regards,
Alicia Gomez
